senses.definition: (of distance or position; also figurative) Extending, reaching or positioned far from a point of reference, especially downwards.

subsenses.definition: Extending far down from the top, or surface, to the bottom, literally or figuratively.
examples: The lake is extremely deep.
We hiked into a deep valley between tall mountains.
There was a deep layer of dust on the floor; the room had not been disturbed for many years.
In the mid-1970s, the economy went into a deep recession.
We are in deep trouble.

subsenses.definition: Positioned far from the surface or other reference point, especially down through something or into something.
examples: Diving down to deep wrecks can be dangerous.

subsenses.definition: Far in extent in another (non-downwards, but generally also non-upwards) direction, especially front-to-back.
examples: The shelves are 30 centimetres deep. — They are deep shelves.
That cyclist's deep chest allows him to draw more air.

subsenses.definition: (in combination) Extending to a level or length equivalent to the stated thing.
examples: The water was waist-deep.
There is an arm-deep hole in the wall.

subsenses.definition: In a (specified) number of rows or layers.
examples: a crowd four deep along the funeral procession, with people two deep on the sidewalks
The fleet of ships was fifty sail deep.
